english_draft: Microsoft reported fiscal Q4 2026 results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, on July 29, 2026. Total revenue was $90.0 billion, up 18% year over year (17% in constant currency). GAAP operating income was $40.6 billion, up 18%. GAAP net income was $35.8 billion, up 31%; non-GAAP net income was $35.3 billion, up 22%. GAAP diluted EPS was $4.81, up 32%; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $4.74, up 23%. Non-GAAP results exclude the impact from investments in OpenAI. Microsoft Cloud revenue was $59.3 billion, up 27%. Commercial remaining performance obligation rose 84% to $678 billion. Productivity and Business Processes revenue was $37.8 billion, up 14%. Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue increased 14% as reported, or 16% adjusted for a prior-year comparable that benefited from 2 points of in-period revenue recognition. Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue increased 24% (22% in constant currency). LinkedIn revenue increased 12% (10% in constant currency). Dynamics 365 revenue increased 13% (12% in constant currency). Intelligent Cloud revenue was $39.3 billion, up 32% (31% in constant currency). Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 43%. More Personal Computing revenue was $12.9 billion, down 4% (5% in constant currency). Windows OEM and Devices revenue decreased 7%. XBOX content and services revenue decreased 10%. Search advertising revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs increased 10% (9% in constant currency). Microsoft returned $10.2 billion to shareholders in dividends and share repurchases in the quarter. The company noted discrete items, including a $3.2 billion gain from its investment in Anthropic and lower-than-expected expenses related to the Voluntary Retirement Program, offset by severance expense and impairment charges in XBOX. These items benefited diluted EPS by $0.27 compared with guidance provided on April 29, 2026. After adjusting for these items, the company said it exceeded expectations across revenue, operating income, and diluted EPS. Fiscal year 2026 revenue was $331.8 billion, up 18% (16% in constant currency). GAAP operating income was $155.2 billion, up 21%. GAAP net income was $133.7 billion, up 31%; non-GAAP net income was $128.8 billion, up 22% (20% in constant currency). GAAP diluted EPS was $17.95, up 32%; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $17.28, up 22% (21% in constant currency). No analyst consensus estimates were included in the source. No comparable preview article written before this earnings release was supplied. Next quarter: management said forward-looking guidance would be provided on the earnings call and webcast on July 29, 2026. The main items to watch are Azure growth, Microsoft 365 Copilot paid seats, capital expenditure trends, and the trajectory of OpenAI-related investment impacts.
reader_questions: The source says non-GAAP adjustments exclude the impact from investments in OpenAI; does the $0.27 benefit of discrete items include the Anthropic gain before or after that exclusion?
Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 43%, but Microsoft Cloud revenue only increased 27%; is the difference explained by segment mix and other cloud components?
The release says the company exceeded expectations after adjusting for discrete items; what were the original guidance numbers for revenue, operating income, and diluted EPS?
fact_checks: Release title, date, and fiscal quarter: Microsoft press release titled "Microsoft Cloud and AI Strength Fuels Fourth Quarter Results," dated July 29, 2026, for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Confirmed.
Basis of presentation: All figures are GAAP unless noted as non-GAAP; non-GAAP excludes the impact from investments in OpenAI. Confirmed in the Non-GAAP Definition section.
Revenue: $90.0 billion (stated as $90,007 million), up 18% GAAP and 17% in constant currency. Confirmed in the constant currency reconciliation table.

Operating income: $40.6 billion (stated as $40,603 million), up 18% GAAP. Confirmed in the constant currency reconciliation table. The release does not present a non-GAAP operating income figure. Noted as a limitation.
Net income: GAAP $35.766 billion, up 31%; non-GAAP $35.286 billion, up 22%. Diluted EPS: GAAP $4.81, up 32%; non-GAAP $4.74, up 23%. Confirmed in the non-GAAP reconciliation table.
Microsoft Cloud revenue: $59.3 billion, up 27%. Confirmed in the Business Highlights section and the constant currency reconciliation.
Commercial remaining performance obligation: increased 84% to $678 billion. Confirmed.

Segment revenue: Productivity and Business Processes $37.847 billion, up 14%; Intelligent Cloud $39.306 billion, up 32% (31% constant currency); More Personal Computing $12.854 billion, down 4% (5% constant currency). Confirmed in the segment reconciliation table.
Azure and other cloud services revenue: increased 43%. Confirmed.

XBOX content and services revenue: decreased 10%. Confirmed. The release attributes the decline to severance expense and impairment charges in XBOX as partial offsets to the discrete benefit items; the release notes "impairment charges in XBOX."

Unusual items: The release states the discrete items versus April 29, 2026 guidance included a $3.2 billion gain from the investment in Anthropic and lower-than-expected Voluntary Retirement Program expenses, partially offset by severance and XBOX impairment charges, resulting in a $0.27 benefit to diluted EPS. Confirmed.
Shareholder returns: $10.2 billion returned in dividends and share repurchases in the fourth quarter. Confirmed.

Fiscal year 2026 totals: Revenue $331.8 billion, up 18% (16% constant currency); operating income $155.2 billion, up 21%; GAAP net income $133.7 billion, up 31%; non-GAAP net income $128.8 billion, up 22% (20% constant currency); GAAP diluted EPS $17.95, up 32%; non-GAAP diluted EPS $17.28, up 22% (21% constant currency). Confirmed in the fiscal year tables.

Guidance and consensus: The release states forward-looking guidance would be provided on the earnings call on July 29, 2026. No numerical guidance figures for Q4 are included in the release, and no analyst consensus figures are included. The statement about exceeding expectations is the company's own characterization; no third-party consensus data are available in the source. Not treated as an independently verified market consensus.
